name: Congenital Anomaly of the Inferior Vena Cava

criteria.description: Visualization of absent or interrupted inferior vena cava on imaging studies (CT, MRI, or venography)
Presence of lower extremity venous insufficiency symptoms such as chronic venous stasis or deep vein thrombosis without other risk factors
Exclusion of acquired causes of inferior vena cava obstruction or thrombosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of IVC anomaly plus clinical presentation consistent with venous insufficiency or thrombosis, excluding acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological supported by clinical findings; genetic testing is not routinely performed.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or interrupted inferior vena cava on imaging
searchTerms: missing or broken lower body vein on scan
absent inferior vena cava on imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Deep vein thrombosis of lower extremities without typical risk factors
pathognomonic.notes: Often presenting symptom in young adults
searchTerms: leg deep vein blood clots without usual causes
unexplained deep vein thrombosis in legs
lower leg clots without risk factors

common.notes: Pain on exertion due to venous insufficiency
In females due to collateral venous pathways

occasional.symptomName: Abdominal pain related to collateral venous engorgement
searchTerms: abdominal discomfort due to vein engorgement
skin color changes on lower legs

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic venous insufficiency
searchTerms: tiredness from poor leg vein flow
fatigue related to chronic venous problems
low energy due to venous insufficiency

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary embolism secondary to deep vein thrombosis
searchTerms: lung blood clot from leg DVT
pulmonary embolism after deep vein thrombosis
lung clot secondary to leg vein clot

rare.symptomName: Lower extremity ulceration due to chronic venous hypertension
searchTerms: leg sores from high vein pressure
chronic venous ulcers on lower legs
skin ulcers due to venous hypertension

laboratory: D-dimer elevation in cases with thrombosis
Normal coagulation profile unless secondary thrombophilia present
imaging: CT or MRI demonstrating absent, interrupted, or hypoplastic inferior vena cava
Ultrasound Doppler revealing altered venous flow in lower extremities
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; etiology largely sporadic
other: Clinical history of unexplained deep vein thrombosis in young patients
Physical exam showing varicosities and edema

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of risk factors for acquired venous obstruction
Imaging shows thrombus or external compression
Compression of left common iliac vein by right common iliac artery
Localized venous obstruction without IVC anomaly

redFlags: Sudden onset of lower limb swelling and pain suggestive of acute deep vein thrombosis
Signs of pulmonary embolism such as dyspnea or chest pain
Progressive venous ulceration or skin necrosis
references: Gayer G, Luboshitz J, Hertz M, Zissin R. Congenital anomalies of the inferior vena cava revealed on CT in patients with deep vein thrombosis. AJR Am J Roentgenol. 2003;180(3):729-732.
